title: fix(app-shell): a page route reads the objects its page binds, not the whole object registry (objectui#12980, part 1)
body:
Part of #12980
Clause-②: yes (widening)

Item 1 of the card only: a page route no longer reads the whole object registry. Items 2 and 3 (the chrome's dashboard and report wave; the bell feeds, agents, timezone and locale reads) come in later claims on the same card. This PR leaves #12980 open.

## What changed

- **`readObjectScope({ names })` with no `packageId` is a names-only scope** (`@object-ui/react`, `MetadataContextValue.readObjectScope` docblock; `MetadataProvider`). Each name is read by name (`GET meta/object/NAME`), with no package list. Only a scope with neither `packageId` nor `names` is the whole registry. No member is added, but the published contract now accepts a call it did not accept before, so `@object-ui/react` is `minor` (the seat's ruling, comment 6252837193). The scope's key is `''`, which no package id can be. A refresh asks its names again, never a package list.
- **`page/:pageName` joins `APP_OBJECT_SCOPE_ROUTES`** (`appObjectScope.ts`). A page route reads the objects its page definition binds, derived from the page by `pageObjectNames`, not from a second hand-written list. The derivation takes the page's `object`, `interfaceConfig.source`, and at any depth every `objectName` and every `dataSource.object`; an `api` data source binds nothing. These objects are read by name, beside the app's package list when the app names a package, or through the names-only scope when it does not. The #12811 rule that sends an app whose package holds no objects to the whole registry does not apply to pages. The chrome gets the same scope. The route waits for the page's own objects. The app's `requiresObject` entries and the lookup targets of the page's objects are read alongside, and the route does not wait for them.
- **`PageView`** reads the same scope (`readPageObjectScope`), never `useMetadata().objects`. When a block asks the page's record navigator about an object outside the set (a lookup target, a list it links to), that object is read by name. `recordHref` / `listHref` answer null until it lands, and the page re-renders when it does. `openRecord` / `openList` navigate once the per-object read answers. A hand-rolled metadata context has no scope, so for it `PageView` reads `objects` as before.
- **The three page blocks:** `InterfaceListPage` reads its source object by name; its record overlay still reads the whole registry once a record is opened, because related lists come from every object. The `nav:menu` capability gate reads the objects its app's entries require, by name: "registered unless the server answered without it", the same rule as the sidebar's #12811 gate. `global:search` reads the registry only once the user types, after `ensureType('object')`.
- The census `openPathObjectReaders-12811` moves `PageView`, `InterfaceListPage` and `nav-menu-renderer` from `off` to `scope`. `global-search-renderer` moves to `action`, which is the honest kind: a search covers every object, so it reads them when a search runs.

## Measurements (the seat's mechanism assumptions)

- **A1:** the server's only bounded list read for `meta/object` is `?package=` (objectstack `meta-collection-routes.ts`, with `createMetaListAnswer` reading only `id`, `object`, `include` and `locale`), plus the per-object GET. There is no names list. The pinned client's `meta.getItems` takes `{ packageId }` only. The two measured control-plane pages (cloud `pricing.page.ts`, `welcome.page.ts`) bind zero objects: every data source is `provider: 'api'`. After this change they read no object at all. Today the page wave waits on at least 50 ms RTT + 307 ms server time, before the 751 KB transfer.
- **A2:** today the route reads the page and the whole registry in parallel (1 wave). Now the page and the app package list (which the chrome reads anyway) load in parallel, and then come the page's bound objects by name. That is 1 wave for a page that binds nothing or only objects its package holds, and 2 waves (about 50 ms + the slowest single read) otherwise. Fewer waves would need the object set before the page has loaded, which the page definition is the only place to get.
- **A3:** the page-route readers that assumed the whole registry, and what each reads now: `AppContent`'s `allObjects` (fed to `ConsoleLayout`, `CommandPalette` and `useTrackRouteAsRecent`) reads the page scope. `PageView` (`ConsoleActionRuntimeProvider`, `RelatedRecordActionsBridge`, the navigator's routable set) reads the page scope plus on-demand reads. `InterfaceListPage`, `nav:menu` and `global:search` are covered above. `useNavMemberGates`, `useServedViewItems` and `useObjectPresence` already read the package scope; see the gap below.

## Tests (at da32c4273c)

- New `AppContent.pageRouteObjects-12980.test.tsx` (real `MetadataProvider`, `AppContent` and `PageView`):
  - (a) a page open asks `object?package=` and, by name, only the bound object outside the package; no `object` call;
  - (a) a page that binds nothing, in an app whose package holds no objects, reads only the package list and the one object a block asked about;
  - (b) CONTROL: the app route's #12811 call set is unchanged;
  - (c) an object a block asks about outside the set is read by name, and its link appears when it lands.
- New `MetadataProvider.namesOnlyScope-12980.test.tsx`: the names-only scope reads by name only, settles and reports `missing`, is cut from a loaded registry without a request, and a refresh asks no package list. CONTROL: `{}` and `{ names: [] }` still mean the whole registry.
- New `pageObjectReads-12980.test.tsx`: `PageView` in an app with no package reads by name only, with the on-demand read and its link. The three blocks each read what they name, with `objects` never read; `global:search` reads only after typing.
- Run: `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=1` over the 58 files that name the touched modules, the census, the route table, the #12811 pins and the scripts suites that read these files: `Test Files 58 passed (58)`, `Tests 571 passed (571)`. `type-check` for `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/react` passed, after a `turbo build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...'` (28/28).
- **Ablation, once:** I took `'page/:pageName'` out of `APP_OBJECT_SCOPE_ROUTES` (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, anchor 1 to 0, blob `e3475fd4` to `567a1e43`). Result: (a) went red twice and (c) went red, while (b) CONTROL stayed green (`Tests 3 failed | 1 passed`). The restore was proven by blob `e3475fd4` equalling HEAD, with `git diff HEAD` empty. The order's literal ablation ("restore `['page','object']`") did not apply: the route table row keeps `['page','object']`, because the record overlay on a page route still waits on the whole registry. The scope-route list is what the change added, so removing it is the equivalent ablation.

## Acceptance notes

- **Gap, not in this surface:** in an app item without `_packageId`, the chrome's `useNavMemberGates`, `useServedViewItems` (the header) and `useObjectPresence` (the bell) still read `objects` on any route, as #12811 left them. A page route in such an app therefore still loads the whole registry through the chrome. The page and its blocks no longer do. The measured control plane carries a package id, so its open is clear.
- A record overlay (`?recordId=`, `?form=`) on a page route reads the whole registry, as on every route.
- Gates (exit 0 each): `pnpm check:` phantom-deps, self-import, unreferenced-sources, doc-example-readers, handler-key-reads, side-effects-array, element-data-source-declaration, spec-symbols, action-forward-parity, designer-field-key-parity, icon-record-names, i18n-keys, i18n-drift, i18n-designer-parity, control-bytes, new-line-citations, test-path-roots; `scripts/check-hand-rolled-comment-mask.mjs`, `check-changeset-fixed.mjs`, `check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`. `eslint` on the 13 changed files: 0 errors. The added warnings are all `no-explicit-any`, in the style of the context's own `any[]` types. The full package directories of `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/react` are declared to CI.
- One `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review is owed before the queue (Clause-②).
